section_summary.extract_value: This Results section reports random assignment checks: ANOVAs showed that only trait levels of body anxiety differed between the experimental conditions, with higher trait body anxiety in the health than appearance conditions (F(1, 125) = 7.19, p = .01; health M = 2.87, SD = 1.09; appearance M = 2.40, SD = 0.98). No other potential covariates (age, BMI, trait endorsement of health or appearance goals, trait introjected regulation) differed significantly between conditions, so those were not treated as differing across conditions.
section_summary.evidence_source: 'Only trait levels of body anxiety significantly varied between conditions; specifically, participants in the health conditions had higher trait levels of body anxiety than those in the appearance conditions, F(1, 125) = 7.19, p = .01; health conditions: M = 2.87, SD = 1.09; appearance conditions: M = 2.40, SD = 0.98.' and 'No other potential covariates varied significantly between conditions (age, BMI, trait endorsement of health or appearance goals, trait introjected regulation; all ps > .05).'
